findings.problem: ShardWorkflow uses `status: String` and `is_sent: bool` / `is_validated: bool` as separate fields. Any combination is legal: a shard can be `status="sent"` with `is_sent=false`, or `status="pending"` with `is_sent=true`, or `status="sent"` with `is_validated=false`. The domain invariant that sent shards must be validated and that status must match flags is not enforced by the type system.
findings.failure_mode: Runtime state corruption: code downstream may check `is_sent` but the shard is not actually in a sent-consistent lifecycle state, or vice versa. Invalid cross-field invariants cause silent data inconsistency.
findings.fix: Replace `status: String`, `is_sent: bool`, `is_validated: bool` with a single `ShardState` enum (e.g., `Pending`, `Validated`, `Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: EpochMs }`). Remove redundant fields entirely so the compiler guarantees valid state combinations.

findings.problem: `id: String` is a bare `String` with no domain constraints. Any arbitrary string is accepted, including empty strings, UUIDs with wrong format, or non-ASCII shard identifiers. No newtype wraps this value.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid shard IDs propagate through the system undetected. Parsing/formatting errors surface at runtime instead of compile time.
findings.fix: Define a `ShardId` newtype with a fallible constructor (e.g., `ShardId::new(s: &str) -> Result<ShardId, InvalidShardId>`) that validates format constraints. Use `ShardId` instead of `String` in `ShardWorkflow`.

findings.problem: `sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64>` is a bare `u64` with no domain meaning. Any u64 value (zero, overflowed, wrong timezone reference) is accepted as a valid epoch timestamp.
findings.failure_mode: Semantically invalid timestamps stored without validation. Arithmetic on raw u64 (e.g., duration calculations) can overflow silently.
findings.fix: Define an `EpochMs` newtype wrapping u64 with a constructor that rejects zero or out-of-range values. Use `EpochMs` in the `ShardState::Sent` variant.

findings.problem: `mark_sent` mutates `ShardWorkflow` in place by accepting and returning the same struct type. It performs field assignment (`item.status = "sent".to_string()`) which is imperative shell behavior leaking into what should be a pure state transition. The function also allocates a new String for status via `.to_string()`.
findings.failure_mode: No guard prevents calling `mark_sent` on an invalid source state (e.g., already-sent or unvalidated shard). The pure computation aspect is lost — the function has observable mutation and allocation side effects instead of returning a new state.
findings.fix: Change signature to `fn mark_sent(state: ShardState) -> Result<ShardState, CannotMarkSent>`. Use a `match` on the source enum variant to only allow the transition from `Validated` to `Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms }`. Return a typed error for disallowed transitions. Eliminate `.to_string()` allocation entirely.

findings.problem: `"sent".to_string()` allocates a new `String` on every call to `mark_sent`. This is an unnecessary heap allocation for a value that should be an enum variant discriminant.
findings.failure_mode: Unbounded allocation in a hot path. Every call to `mark_sent` leaks one heap allocation with zero lifetime benefit if the status is never read back as a string.
findings.fix: Replace `status: String` with an enum discriminant. The state transition returns the target enum variant with zero heap allocation.

findings.problem: `id: String` means every `ShardWorkflow` owns its id on the heap. No borrowed or zero-copy alternative is used at the boundary.
findings.failure_mode: Excessive heap allocations for shard records that may be created and discarded frequently. No `Cow<str>` or `&str` borrowing path exists for read-only access patterns.
findings.fix: Use a `ShardId` newtype that can internally use `Cow<'static, str>` for small/fixed-length shard IDs, or parse into `ShardId` at the boundary and store the validated type.

findings.problem: The struct has three independent boolean/string flags (`status`, `is_validated`, `is_sent`) instead of a typestate. A consumer cannot express in the type that "only validated shards can be sent" — they must check invariants manually at every call site.
findings.failure_mode: Every caller must remember to check `is_validated && is_sent` consistency manually. Missing checks lead to state machine violations that are only caught by integration tests.
findings.fix: Define `enum ShardState { Pending, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: EpochMs } }`. Transitions are methods on the enum that enforce allowed transitions at compile time. `Pending` cannot be sent without first becoming `Validated`.

no profiler evidence for allocation patterns in mark_sent
no allocation audit (no `try_reserve` or capacity analysis present)
no behavior test for valid state transitions (pending->validated->sent)
no behavior test for invalid state transitions (pending->sent directly)
no command evidence (no cargo test/cargo fmt/cargo clippy output)
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The core issue is architectural: the entire type system is primitive-based with no domain invariants. Without an enum-based typestate, no amount of arithmetic or allocation fixes can make illegal states unrepresentable. The crate needs a complete type-level redesign before any performance or safety micro-fixes are meaningful.
